result.title: When Reasoning Goes Astray: Attention Dynamics of Uncontrolled Reasoning
result.summary: Large reasoning models (LRMs) improve performance on complex tasks through extended reasoning, yet the same process can degenerate into redundant verification and persistent generation loops. Such uncontrolled reasoning increases inference cost and creates risks of resource exhaustion and service degradation. However, existing mitigations largely truncate long outputs or react to surface repetition, and thus fail to distinguish normal thinking from uncontrolled reasoning or explain how benign reasoning degenerates into harmful behavior. In this paper, we operationalize LRM generation as four states and further introduce Reasoning-state Analysis via Dynamic Attention Responses (RADAR), which identifies the current reasoning state in real time and characterizes how effective reflection can develop into uncontrolled generation. Guided by RADAR's analysis, we further realign abnormal attention distributions toward patterns observed in normal requests and examine how this correction affects excessive reflection and persistent looping. Temporal analyses show that uncontrolled reasoning is characterized by attention distributions that deviate from normal generation, with abnormal trends becoming detectable before repetition begins. Correcting these deviations through Attention Realignment consistently reduces looping while largely preserving benign performance. Together, RADAR provide a mechanistic account of how reasoning becomes uncontrolled, offering actionable guidance for identifying critical failure stages and designing targeted runtime interventions.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文将大推理模型的生成过程刻画为四种推理状态，提出 RADAR 方法，通过动态注意力响应实时判别当前状态，并据此把异常注意力分布校正回正常模式，以缓解冗余验证与持续循环。
AI.relevance_reason: 虽为纯文本 LRM 研究，但其「状态判别 + 何时停止思考 + 注意力分布何时偏离」的框架，可能为 LVR 中的 STOP 决策与 latent 状态的注意力/位置结构分析提供线索，尤其异常信号先于重复出现的现象值得对照核查。
